source_correspondence: H0 states the full spatial metric, zero Dirichlet condition, support of both Cauchy jets and uniform distribution bounds for every parameter derivative. The conclusion uses one fixed parameter neighborhood for every mixed derivative, with order-dependent constants.

F0 uses a boundary-preserving fixed linear isometry and parameter-dependent center translation. The metric-ball containment includes a first-exit argument excluding shortcuts outside the controlled coefficient region.

F1 proves both time orientations of finite propagation through positive shrinking-cone flux. Every cone remains in the region of controlled coefficients; the physical boundary and all complex lower terms are retained.

N0 normalizes the whole family before differentiation. Its flow leaves physical time and the normal coordinate unchanged, and the full density, positive normalizing factor and complex gauge yield an exact monic normal equation. The target and common zero-region margins are quantitative.

N1 writes the complete binomial parameter system. Every source coefficient derivative is tangential. Flat-test transposition and the original parameter-distribution bounds give a finite negative Sobolev order for each finite collection of parameter derivatives.

O0 refines the actual CRO proof so the full observation input lies inside the zero region. Its countable tests, full residual comparisons and output-only scalar relocation preserve that support; microsupport alone is not used to infer a vanishing observation.

O1 fixes the cutoff and coarse order before the tested estimate. Its complete input margin makes the differential cutoff commutator vanish. Full compositions with the parameter derivatives of R retain all residuals, finite order and bounded parameter seminorms.

G0 gives the full flat reflected and gliding geometry, a 7/100 observation margin and a 363/100 spatial travel bound. G1 proves compact segment stability for every continuation, with physical-time transversality and one parameter neighborhood before derivative orders.

G2 constructs compact tubes closed under all backward continuations and endpoint observation buffers. Each compact target closure lies strictly inside a larger open access neighborhood, as required by CRO. Infinite-contact continuation is never selected uniquely.

I0 proves finite parameter induction for arbitrary bounded full target families. The exact source compositions are controlled on the preceding larger cone. Neighborhoods may depend on parameter derivative order, not on target order.

J0 uses genuine polynomial tangential differential tests, exact mixed normal-recovery indices and a finite ordinary-normal recurrence. It proves all ordinary boundary jets and pointwise bounds without assuming that b-regularity by itself gives ordinary normal regularity.

J1 takes a finite parameter cover separately for each derivative order over the same compact parameter set, then returns through the full inverse coordinate chain rule. It never intersects infinitely many shrinking parameter neighborhoods.

The three complete solutions verify a reflected ray, a shear removing the original mixed-normal parameter forcing, and a one-dimensional odd wave with the correct normalized source sign. Physical time provides positive tangential dimension even in one spatial dimension.

This delivers the full wave application under the stated family and Cauchy-support hypotheses. General manifold scalar assembly, remaining general-observation dimension cases, sharp general Airy mapping and all remaining course obligations stay active. External human proofs remain external.
